candidates.title: [Bug]: toString/println ignore an object's own toString() method and print `object`
candidates.body:
### Description
`value:toString` (and therefore `io:println` and the informal rendering of list members) renders an object whose class defines `toString()` as `object` instead of calling that method. Calling `p.toString()` directly works, so it is the ToString abstract operation that ignores the user-defined method.

### Steps to Reproduce
Run `go run ./cli/cmd run repro.bal` with:

```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

class Point {
    int x = 3;
    public function toString() returns string {
        return "P(" + self.x.toString() + ")";
    }
}

public function main() {
    Point p = new;
    any a = p;
    io:println(a.toString()); // @output P(3)
    io:println(p); // @output P(3)
    any[] arr = [p];
    io:println(arr.toString()); // @output [P(3)]
}
```

**Actual output**
```
object
object
[object]
```

**Expected output**
```
P(3)
P(3)
[P(3)]
```

**Spec reasoning**
Spec §5.9.5 (ToString), row *object with toString method*: informal and direct style are `S`, "where S is the result of calling the toString method". The list row renders members in informal style (`[X,Y]`). lang.value `toString`: "The details of the conversion are specified by the ToString abstract operation ... using the direct style." So `a.toString()` and `arr.toString()` must give `P(3)` / `[P(3)]`; `io:println(p)` follows by convention.

### Affected Version(s)
`main` @ cc62d6d68b9330e342c17d466d915e5064b02528

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux; built from ballerina-nutcracker/ballerina `main` (cc62d6d68b9330e342c17d466d915e5064b02528) with `go run ./cli/cmd run <file.bal>`.

### Related area
Runtime

### Related issue(s) (optional)
#979 (objects *without* toString should render as `object D1&D2 U`) says the with-toString case was handled via #839; this reproducer shows it is not (likely an unwired path in `values/values.go` toString/BalString for `*Object`).

candidates.title: [Bug]: error values print the constructor's type name (alias/intersection) instead of their type-ids
candidates.body:
### Description
When an error is constructed via an alias of a distinct error type, or via an intersection of distinct error types, its string form uses the name written in the error constructor rather than the error's type-ids. `a is MyErr` is true, yet it prints `error Alias (...)`.

### Steps to Reproduce
Run `go run ./cli/cmd run repro.bal` with:

```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

type MyErr distinct error;
type Other distinct error;
type Alias MyErr;
type Both MyErr & Other;

public function main() {
    Alias a = error Alias("x");
    io:println(a); // @output error MyErr ("x")
    Both b = error Both("y");
    io:println(b); // @output error MyErr&Other ("y")
}
```

**Actual output**
```
error Alias ("x")
error Both ("y")
```

**Expected output**
```
error MyErr ("x")
error MyErr&Other ("y")
```

**Spec reasoning**
§5.1.5 Type-ids: "The set of type-ids of an object or error value are those induced by the type-descriptor used to construct it." A type-reference induces the same type-ids as the type it refers to (so `Alias` induces {MyErr}; only `distinct` creates a type-id). §5.7.8: an intersection T1&T2 "induces the union of the set of type-ids induced by T1 and T2". §6.17: "The type-ids of the constructed error value are those induced by E." §5.9.5 error row: `error D1&D2 (M,...)` where informal/direct use the local ids of the type-ids. The order of `MyErr&Other` is not fixed by the spec (`Other&MyErr` is also conforming); the `Alias` line is unambiguous.

### Affected Version(s)
`main` @ cc62d6d68b9330e342c17d466d915e5064b02528

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux; built from ballerina-nutcracker/ballerina `main` (cc62d6d68b9330e342c17d466d915e5064b02528) with `go run ./cli/cmd run <file.bal>`.

### Related area
Runtime

### Related issue(s) (optional)
#1350 (closed) fixed non-distinct `type E error;` printing `E`; the fix appears to still use the constructor's reference name rather than the actual type-ids.

[Bug]: xml:strip drops whitespace-only text adjacent to a comment/PI instead of merging chunks first
candidates.body:
### Description
`xml:strip` judges each text item on its own while comments/processing instructions are still present. After removing comments/PIs the adjacent text items should merge, and only chunks that are entirely whitespace should be removed. The bug is in `strip` itself: building the value as `xml`a` + xml`<!--c-->` + xml` `` and calling `.strip()` also prints `[a]`.

### Steps to Reproduce
Run `go run ./cli/cmd run repro.bal` with:

```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

public function main() {
    xml x = xml `a<!--c--> `;
    io:println("[", x.strip(), "]"); // @output [a ]
    xml y = xml ` <?p?>b`;
    io:println("[", y.strip(), "]"); // @output [ b]
    xml z = xml `<e/> <!--c--> x <!--d--> <f/>`;
    io:println("[", z.strip(), "]"); // @output [<e/>  x  <f/>]
}
```

**Actual output**
```
[a]
[b]
[<e/> x <f/>]
```

**Expected output**
```
[a ]
[ b]
[<e/>  x  <f/>]
```

**Spec reasoning**
lang.xml `strip`: it "first transforms the xml value by leaving out any constituent item that is a comment or processing instruction. It then transforms this value by leaving out any constituent item that is a text item that consists entirely of whitespace" ("the text is grouped into the biggest possible chunks (i.e., only elements cause division into multiple chunks)"). §5.3.2: "When an xml value is constructed, consecutive text singletons are merged, so that an xml value never contains consecutive text singletons." So after step 1, `"a"` and `" "` form one text item `"a "`, which is not all whitespace and must be kept.

### Affected Version(s)
`main` @ cc62d6d68b9330e342c17d466d915e5064b02528

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux; built from ballerina-nutcracker/ballerina `main` (cc62d6d68b9330e342c17d466d915e5064b02528) with `go run ./cli/cmd run <file.bal>`.

### Related area
Runtime

### Related issue(s) (optional)
#1453 (template drops whitespace after a PI) is a different, parser-level bug; this reproducer's `y` case keeps its leading space before `strip` and is not affected by it.

candidates.title: [Bug]: xml value interpolated into an xml template is re-parsed, taking the outer default namespace and losing identity
candidates.body:
### Description
An `xml` value inserted into an XML template via `${...}` is serialized and re-parsed as part of the template text. As a result the inserted element is captured by the enclosing default namespace (its name changes from `i` to `{urn:o}i`) and it becomes a copy rather than the same element (`===` is false). Relatedly, `wrapped` prints as `<o xmlns="urn:o"><i/></o>` instead of `<o xmlns="urn:o"><i xmlns=""/></o>` (§5.3.2.1: an `xmlns=""` AII is added when the element has no namespace but a default namespace is in scope).

### Steps to Reproduce
Run `go run ./cli/cmd run repro.bal` with:

```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

public function main() {
    xml:Element inner = xml `<i/>`;
    xml wrapped = xml `<o xmlns="urn:o">${inner}</o>`;
    if wrapped is xml:Element {
        xml:Element child = <xml:Element>wrapped.getChildren().get(0);
        io:println(child.getName()); // @output i
        io:println(child === inner); // @output true
    }
}
```

**Actual output**
```
{urn:o}i
false
```

**Expected output**
```
i
true
```

**Spec reasoning**
§6.6.2: the template literal is parsed and converted into an xml value, then "A new copy is made of the xml value and the result of the expression evaluations are inserted into the corresponding position in the newly created xml value." Only the template's own value is copied; nothing renames or copies the inserted value, and namespace processing applies to the literal parts only, so `inner`'s expanded name stays `i`. §5.3.2: "Singleton element, processing instruction and comment values have storage identity"; §5.3: when a constituent has storage identity "what is stored in the sequence value is a reference to the location where the constituent value is stored". Hence `child === inner` must be `true`.

### Affected Version(s)
`main` @ cc62d6d68b9330e342c17d466d915e5064b02528

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux; built from ballerina-nutcracker/ballerina `main` (cc62d6d68b9330e342c17d466d915e5064b02528) with `go run ./cli/cmd run <file.bal>`.

### Related area
Runtime

### Related issue(s) (optional)
#1092 (closed) shows the same splice-into-text-and-re-parse mechanism (`evalTemplate[xml]`), there only for attribute string escaping.
